The sediment follows: 70% and more than 92% trapped under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% removed over natural events [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3] with a worst-case floor of 71% and 86% across all storms [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in the Kansas plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a corn strip was restored to fescue in Connecticut [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1], and fairly narrow strips of riparian vegetation reducing sediment input across the field studies reviewed [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15]. Widening the Prince Edward Island buffers from the present 15 m to 100 m is modelled to retain a further 30.5 to 36.2% of the stream sediment load [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1]. Roots hold the bank itself: forested buffer strips stabilise banks more effectively than grass [ev_streambank_erosion_osbo93_17], willow posts limited further loss to an additional 0.3 m of bank through the 1993 floods, and streambank integrity was maintained on the planted reach [ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_2].

justification.mechanism: Three pathways carry this effect. Sediment-bound load settles out in the strip: 70% and more than 92% of incoming sediment trapped under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in pumped-runoff plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], and 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a cropped riparian strip was seeded to fescue [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]. Vadose-zone nitrate inside the Iowa buffer never exceeded 2 mg per litre while the adjacent fields exceeded 12 [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1]. Restoring a cropped Connecticut strip to fescue cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen by 70%, nitrate by 83%, total phosphorus by 73% and suspended solids by 92%, and groundwater nitrate by 35% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2, ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]. effect_mechanism: A planted strip works by settling, infiltration and uptake. Sediment-bound load is trapped: 70% and more than 92% of incoming sediment under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events with a floor of 71% and 86% [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in the Kansas plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], 97% behind an 8 m fescue strip and 91% within the first 4 m [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4], and 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a cropped strip was seeded to fescue [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1]. Dissolved load is removed as water passes through: across 88 buffers, mean nitrogen removal effectiveness was 67.5%, at 0.394 mg per litre per metre [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_2]; the Bear Creek plantings removed 80% and 94% of total nitrogen over natural events and 64 to 93% under a 25 mm per hour simulation [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_5, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_9, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1]; a seeded Connecticut strip cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen by 70%, nitrate by 83% and total phosphorus by 73% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]; grass strips reduced nitrate in surface runoff by 54-84%, phosphorus by 61-83% and subsurface nitrogen by 10-60%, and 80 to 90% nitrate reduction was found in subsurface water after passage through grass and forest strips [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_11, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_13, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_9, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_4]; and nutrients are locked into the planted biomass, 770 and 90 kg of nitrogen per hectare in the Quebec poplar buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_1]. Planted canopy also shades the water: wooded strips moderate diel temperature fluctuations, and buffers significantly reduced post-harvest temperature increases, with partially cut 10-20 m strips still shading the stream [ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_2, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3].
conditionality: Planting does not guarantee a sink. Narrow buffers under 15 m actually contributed nitrogen to the riparian zone in six of the pooled studies [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_3], buffer outflow in the early stages of a natural runoff event can contribute pollutants to surface waters [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_5], and in the Connecticut restoration total Kjeldahl nitrogen and total phosphorus increased significantly as groundwater passed through the restored strip while the other groundwater nitrogen species did not respond [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_3, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_4]; part of that site's groundwater nitrate decline was due to the cessation of fertilisation rather than the planting [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2], and its authors warn that early-stage restoration may deliver much less than established buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]. Mass is not concentration — 91.8 and 92.1% mass reductions against 42.9 and 44.4% in concentration, dissolved phosphorus down only 16%, nitrate 10-19% against 48-72% for ammonium [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_4] — and intensity removes the soluble benefit: at 69 mm per hour removal fell to 50 and 28% and to 35% for phosphate behind the wider buffer, phosphate mass was not significantly reduced at that intensity, and soluble removal held above 60% in every storm but the most intense [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_6, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_7, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_8, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8]. Texture limits the sediment pathway, at 52% retention of clay against 93% of sand and silt and 35% on silty clay loam where sandy loam was almost 100% [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2]; extra width adds little, with only 4.6 and 4.0% gained in modelling from 50 m to 100 m, and 30 m buffers failed to prevent increased stream sedimentation after partial clearcutting [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2]. Nearly all of it is plot-scale or modelled temperate high-income work — Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, Connecticut, Prince Edward Island, a UK review and a pooled analysis that states no study country — with the Bear Creek reach measured repeatedly across related studies; none of it is a planted buffer measured in a low-income farming system.

justification.mechanism: A planted strip works by settling, infiltration and uptake. Sediment-bound load is trapped: 70% and more than 92% of incoming sediment under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events with a floor of 71% and 86% [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in the Kansas plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], 97% behind an 8 m fescue strip and 91% within the first 4 m [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4], and 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a cropped strip was seeded to fescue [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1]. Dissolved load is removed as water passes through: across 88 buffers, mean nitrogen removal effectiveness was 67.5%, at 0.394 mg per litre per metre [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_2]; the Bear Creek plantings removed 80% and 94% of total nitrogen over natural events and 64 to 93% under a 25 mm per hour simulation [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_5, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_9, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1]; a seeded Connecticut strip cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen by 70%, nitrate by 83% and total phosphorus by 73% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]; grass strips reduced nitrate in surface runoff by 54-84%, phosphorus by 61-83% and subsurface nitrogen by 10-60%, and 80 to 90% nitrate reduction was found in subsurface water after passage through grass and forest strips [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_11, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_13, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_9, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_4]; and nutrients are locked into the planted biomass, 770 and 90 kg of nitrogen per hectare in the Quebec poplar buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_1]. Planted canopy also shades the water: wooded strips moderate diel temperature fluctuations, and buffers significantly reduced post-harvest temperature increases, with partially cut 10-20 m strips still shading the stream [ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_2, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3].
justification.conditionality: Planting does not guarantee a sink. Narrow buffers under 15 m actually contributed nitrogen to the riparian zone in six of the pooled studies [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_3], buffer outflow in the early stages of a natural runoff event can contribute pollutants to surface waters [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_5], and in the Connecticut restoration total Kjeldahl nitrogen and total phosphorus increased significantly as groundwater passed through the restored strip while the other groundwater nitrogen species did not respond [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_3, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_4]; part of that site's groundwater nitrate decline was due to the cessation of fertilisation rather than the planting [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2], and its authors warn that early-stage restoration may deliver much less than established buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]. What you plant decides the result: a 20 m oat buffer had no significant effect on total phosphorus where a 10 m rye grass strip did [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_4, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5], the grass strip did little to reduce phosphorus in shallow groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_3], and at the least fertile Quebec site the planted poplars accumulated no more nitrogen than the unmanaged herbaceous buffer beside them [ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_2]. Mass is not concentration — 91.8 and 92.1% mass reductions against 42.9 and 44.4% in concentration, dissolved phosphorus down only 16%, nitrate 10-19% against 48-72% for ammonium [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_4] — and intensity removes the soluble benefit: at 69 mm per hour removal fell to 50 and 28% and to 35% for phosphate behind the wider buffer, phosphate mass was not significantly reduced at that intensity, and soluble removal held above 60% in every storm but the most intense [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_6, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_7, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_8, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8]. Performance also decays: the effectiveness of wooded buffers typically diminishes over time as the nutrient requirements of trees decrease with age [ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_7]. The thermal benefit can invert — newly restored streams whose canopy was removed during construction had higher temperatures [ev_stream_temperature_mcmi14_1] — and that urban study, bundled with channel regrading, rests on a sample of three for its nitrate result, with its phosphate comparison not significant [ev_nutrient_removal_mcmi14_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mcmi14_2]. Texture limits the sediment pathway, at 52% retention of clay against 93% of sand and silt and 35% on silty clay loam where sandy loam was almost 100% [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2]; extra width adds little, with only 4.6 and 4.0% gained in modelling from 50 m to 100 m, and 30 m buffers failed to prevent increased stream sedimentation after partial clearcutting [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2]. Nearly all of it is plot-scale or modelled temperate high-income work — Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, Connecticut, Prince Edward Island, a UK review and a pooled analysis that states no study country — with the Bear Creek reach measured repeatedly across related studies; none of it is a planted buffer measured in a low-income farming system.
